item.title: Sakaide and the Seto Ohashi Bridge Gateway — Guide
item.description: Sakaide, on the Kagawa coast west of Takamatsu, is the Shikoku-side gateway of the Great Seto Bridge (Seto Ohashi), the mighty road-and-rail bridge system that leaps across the Seto Inland Sea to connect Shikoku with Honshu. The bridge — actually a series of long spans hopping between islands — is an engineering marvel and a landmark of the region, best appreciated from viewpoints, memorial parks and the tower at its foot.

item.title: Washuzan Hill: The Seto Ohashi Bridge Viewpoint — Guide
item.description: Washuzan is a modest hill of just 133 metres on the southern coast of Kurashiki, but its view is one of the finest in western Japan. From its granite outcrops the whole eastern Seto Inland Sea opens out below: dozens of green islands scattered across the water, ships threading between them, and the vast Seto Ohashi bridge striding across the strait to Shikoku on a series of enormous suspension spans. It is celebrated as one of Japan’s great sunset spots, when the sea turns gold and the bridge is silhouetted, and later the bridge itself is illuminated.
